findings.message: The `if [[ "$rc" -eq 10 ]]` turn-budget branch is unreachable in production: route_to_model documents exit codes {0,1,2} (plus 124/137 passthrough, core/router/route.sh:109,1133-1136); its budget-exhaustion path sets _ROUTE_LAST_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED=1 and returns 1, never 10 (rc=10 is `plan`'s unrelated scope_too_large abort code, scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh:54). A real turn-budget exhaustion during monitor's route_to_model call therefore falls into the generic rc-nonzero branch, where _ROUTE_LAST_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED also can't be observed (it was set inside the $(route_to_model ...) subshell and never propagates to the caller), so the written result is disposition:unavailable/reason:router_rc_nonzero, not out_of_turns/budget_exhausted. SPEC-24 only passes because its test mocks route_to_model to literally return rc=10.

Pre-existing identical dead-code pattern: `if [[ "$router_rc" -eq 10 ]]` checks for a route_to_model return value that function never produces, so review-lens's own out_of_turns/budget_exhausted branch is equally unreachable today. This diff's monitor branch copies this same broken convention rather than introducing a novel bug class.

`_mon_start_s="$SECONDS"` is read and immediately subtracted from `$SECONDS` on the next line with no intervening work, so `_budget_elapsed_s` is always 0 and the WALL CLOCK BUDGET block always reports "~0s have elapsed" regardless of real elapsed time.

`trap '_monitor_interrupt_handler' TERM INT` clobbers whatever TERM/INT handler the calling process already had installed (e.g. the runner's established re-arm handler per #1759/#1860) without saving it first, and `trap - TERM INT` on line 191 resets the disposition to default rather than restoring the prior handler — so if plugin.sh's functions are sourced into the runner's own process (as the dispatch convention comment implies), any SIGTERM/SIGINT delivered after this window (during subsequent report-writing, cleanup hooks, or later stages sharing the process) now gets the OS default action instead of whatever graceful handling existed before, silently weakening the engine's shutdown/cleanup guarantees for the remainder of the process lifetime.

deploy_result_json/pr_url_txt paths are taken verbatim from ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS and dereferenced (`-f` test, `jq -c .`, file read) with no check that the resolved path stays within the expected state/artifacts directory; their content is then folded into the model prompt with only route_to_model's generic redaction as a backstop, so any path an upstream/engine component places in that index gets read off disk and sent to the external model.

`_mon_out_ref` and `_mon_interrupted` are assigned without `local`, so they leak into the enclosing shell/global namespace; harmless under the current single-invocation-per-process dispatch model but a latent footgun if monitor_stage_run is ever invoked more than once in the same sourced shell (e.g. retried in-process, or reused by a future harness change), since a signal racing the very first assignment on a later call would still see the previous run's stale `_mon_out_ref`.
File mode changed from 100755 to 100644 with no content change at all; this file is unrelated to the monitor v2 migration and is not in the design's declared file scope.
File mode changed from 100755 to 100644 alongside the SPEC-13 assertion addition; the permission change is incidental and this file is not in the design's declared scope list.
File mode changed from 100755 to 100644 alongside the new SPEC-10/11/12/17/18 guard assertions; the content additions fit the migration but the permission-bit flip is an incidental, unrequested edit.

The new rc=130 (interrupted) and rc=10 (out_of_turns) exit branches write the v2 result and a stage summary but never call emit_event "monitor.alert", unlike every other failure path in this function (generic router failure, unparseable response, verdict!=pass) — the two failure modes this ADR-063 migration exists to surface are the ones excluded from monitor's own declared alerting event.

trap '_monitor_interrupt_handler' TERM INT is unconditionally cleared with `trap - TERM INT` after route_to_model returns, resetting to the OS default handler rather than restoring whatever trap (if any) the caller had installed before monitor_stage_run ran, so any outer signal handling in scope for the remainder of this stage's process lifetime is silently dropped.
